summary: Gone 1940s live-in tower on Reed Hill, Grays Harbor County, WA; removed or destroyed 1963; footing and concrete reported near the summit.

facts.design: live-in fire tower, built in the 1940s per the register
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1963. A National Geodetic Survey station description on the history page, dated 1964, says the lookout tower has been removed.

staffing.status: seasonal fire-season staffing; closed for the season in September 1951 and on September 8, 1952

access.note: Road is gated at the paved Wynoochee Valley Road. The trip report describes a bike or walk up through gates; part of the south slopes is private land.

visit.trail_note: About 6 miles with 1,000 ft of climb; the trip report recommends biking. Road gated at the paved Wynoochee Valley Road, about 20 miles from Montesano (firelookout.com says 23 miles).

facts.agency: Washington Division of Forestry/DNR; operated for fire detection by the Simpson Logging Company in 1944 (AWS report)

events.note: Listed as activated August 9, 1942 (Olympia Filter Center)
AWS report dated May 1, 1944 lists it as a private Simpson Logging Co. station operated for fire detection, named Baker 9-1
Closed for the season in September 1951 when its lookout left for college
Closed September 8, 1952 for the season; ocean fog made the lookouts useless
Register says removed in 1963; firelookout.com and the trip report say destroyed in 1963
NGS station description, described 1964, says the lookout tower has been removed
A recent harvest opened up the entire summit area

notes_for_editor: Brief coordinates, elevation (440 m) and FFLOS registration match; no corrections. Removal year 1963 agrees across all three sources (register says removed, the other two say destroyed). The NGS station description on the Weebly page (described 1964) says the tower was removed but gives no removal date, so the story does not date it. Names of the 1951 and 1952 lookouts are omitted. A trip report photo caption, 'Possible metal from a lookout', is not used. The 1944 AWS report calls the station a 'private station'; the Weebly ownership line reads 'Simpson Logging Co. > Department of Natural Resources'. Access level 'restricted' rests on the gated road and private land; check before going. No WebSearch used; four cached pages read. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story now calls the NGS item a station description, not a recovery note, and notes firelookout.com's 23-mile distance. 'Under debris' is the trip report's 'under the debres' (typo). The 1951 closure is tied to the staffer leaving for college, as the item says.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1951 item (Weebly) puts the lookout about 20 miles north of Montesano, and the trip report puts the gate about 20 miles from Montesano. firelookout.com says 23 miles north. The story gives 20 and notes 23.
